channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [Financial Times] Democrats pledge to expose ‘absolute avalanche of corruption’ under Trump
item.description: Congress member Jamie Raskin says he will launch sweeping probe of president and allies but warns party to avoid impeachment ‘distraction’

item.title: [EU Observer] The olive branch is a universal symbol of peace – but the West Bank’s autumn olive harvest is open season for Israeli settlers to pillage and kill
item.description: The olive has become much more than a household staple. In Palestine, the annual autumn harvest requires courage, protection by activists and an often deadly struggle. The contrast to Europe's olive tradition has never been so stark.

item.title: [DW] Wael Mohya could make German football history at 17
item.description: At just 17, Gladbach forward Wael Mohya has earned his first Germany call-up. The dual-national talent has chosen the DFB path for now — and could soon make modern national-team history.

item.title: [EU Observer] War of propaganda: Russia calls Ukraine a ‘burden’ and uses Moldova as a ‘testing ground’ to sabotage EU enlargement
item.description: From fake celebrity sex scandals to ominous warnings about land seizures and soaring bills, Kremlin-linked campaigns are working to turn ordinary voters against EU accession long before any referendum is held.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] ‘I cannot be optimistic,’ says climatologist Jean Jouzel
item.description: Jean Jouzel, a renowned French climatologist, is not optimistic about the changing climate and the level of mitigation efforts. But he says people should should not give up on the fight against global warming.

item.title: [EU Observer] First talks about EU envoy on Ukraine war to dominate Dublin summits
item.description: Even a Nobel prize-winning expert, Geoffrey Hinton, who is known as the "Godfather of AI", might struggle to hold the room's attention, as EU leaders focus on how to handle the latest US push to end the Ukrainian war.

item.title: [DW] British counterterrorism police arrest US soldier accused of spying on behalf of Russia
item.description: A member of the US Army has been arrested near Gloucester in England. Police said he was suspected of espionage activity in connection with Russia. Investigators from the US and UK are involved in the probe.

item.title: [DW] UK Privy Council overrules Trinidad and Tobago gay sex law
item.description: A London court has overturned a Trinidad and Tobago law criminalizing consensual sexual relations between male same-sex couples. As a result of the colonial legacy, it is the independent country's last court of appeal.

item.title: [DW] Victims of Nazi war in Poland call on Germany for support
item.description: More than 80 years after the end of World War II, Polish victims of the Nazi regime are still waiting for a "humanitarian gesture" from Germany. The 2027 draft budget hasn't left them much hope for possible reparations.

item.title: [DW] Iran denies role in fridge hack, France summons ambassador
item.description: France has said it rules "nothing" out in response to a cyberattack on supermarket refrigeration units. Iran, however, said it categorically rejected Paris' "baseless and one-sided accusations" of IRGC involvement.

item.title: [DW] Bulgaria highway pileup kills 12, dozens injured: PM
item.description: At least 12 people were killed and dozens injured in a series of crashes caused by thick fog in Bulgaria. Police, firefighters and paramedics were dispatched to the scene for the rescue operation.

item.title: [DW] Fact check: Online disinformation rife after Krakow mass shooting
item.description: Fake and AI-manipulated images spread online in the hours after the Krakow attack, fueling false narratives about the mass shooting. DW Fact Check examined what's real, and what isn't.

item.title: [DW] US, Russia, Ukraine wrap up talks with prisoner exchange agreement
item.description: Peace talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US concluded in the United Arab Emirates. The two day talks were the first such meeting since February. DW has the latest updates.

item.title: [EU Observer] Europe’s self-styled pacifists are helping Putin freeze Ukrainians in their homes
item.description: As Russia bombs Ukraine’s grid, Hungary, Slovakia, the Czech Republic and Bulgaria want to opt out of the next EU loan - money that actually also helps Ukrainian's civilians build back-up power and heating.

item.title: [Financial Times] Nvidia sends a painful message on how to value a CEO
item.description: More clarity about why founders matter — and how much — should help everyone

item.title: [Politico Europe] Climate science says 1.5C is dead. No one wants to bury it.
item.description: Leaders at COP31 want to keep the totemic goal alive, even after the U.N. declared it impossible to hit.

item.title: [DW] Czechia braces for massive protest as anger over government's public media reform plans boils
item.description: A fast-tracked bill on public media funding reform has sparked strikes, rallies and fears for the independence of public broadcasting in Czechia. A massive protest is due to take place in Prague on November 15.

item.title: [Financial Times] US home sales fall to lowest level since 2010 as mortgage rates soar
item.description: Higher borrowing costs deepen housing market slump as interest rates weigh on transactions

item.title: [Euractiv] Croatia brushes off pressure to go easy on Montenegro
item.description: Andrej Plenković says he is stalling Podgorcia's membership bid to defend 'EU values'

item.title: [Euractiv] MIDTERMS: ECR opens hunting season on cordon sanitaire
item.description: European Conservatives and Reformists (ECR) uses backing for Green candidate to demand that rules are respected

item.title: [EU Observer] EU Parliament asked to lift immunity of German far-right MEP accused of baseball‑bat attack on teen
item.description: The EU parliament was requested to waive a German far-right MEP’s immunity to allow his prosecution for drunk-driving and violently assaulting minors with a baseball bat.

item.title: [Financial Times] European leaders reject Russian push to overhaul continent’s security
item.description: ‘Europe needs to pay attention’, warns Zelenskyy after Abu Dhabi talks

item.title: [Financial Times] Quantum Systems drones grounded by German military after cyber attack
item.description: Start-up with €7bn valuation and operations in Ukraine is latest European arms group to be targeted

item.title: [EU Observer] With Russia’s front collapsing, Putin is weaponising the Dnipro River by using it to slice Ukraine in two (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,722)
item.description: Ukraine’s commanders warn that if bridges fall, cities are evacuated and Patriots stay empty, the war could shift from the front lines to a desperate race to stop a 1,000‑km river from becoming an internal border.

item.title: [Financial Times] Meet the contenders to succeed Jensen Huang
item.description: From chief executives of rival companies to the former CEO’s own children, the race to lead Nvidia has begun

item.title: [Politico Europe] De grandes villes européennes demandent à l’UE d’interdire les filtres des cigarettes
item.description: De Bruxelles à Dublin, des municipalités ont rejoint la campagne No (Plastic) Filter, qui mise sur deux lois européennes en cours de révision pour interdire les filtres, ou au moins le plastique qu’ils contiennent.

item.title: [DW] Can the EU make it harder to trick consumers online?
item.description: The EU wants to curb subscription traps, misleading sales tactics and features that keep people scrolling. What would the proposed Digital Fairness Act change, and does it go far enough?

item.title: [Politico Europe] COP 31 : qu’attendre des négociations ?
item.description: Le président Lula a été accueilli sous les applaudissements à son arrivée, mercredi, à la COP 31 qui se tient à Antalya, en Turquie. Mais mis à part le Brésilien et quelques autres, de nombreux chefs d’Etats et de gouvernement, dont ceux de la France, de l’Allemagne ou de l’Inde ont fait l’impasse sur cette […]

item.title: [Euractiv] No MFF, no Christmas
item.description: Also, in tonight’s edition: Europe's continued struggle over who should talk to Russia

item.title: [EU Observer] EU’s Kallas wants next week’s UK‑EU summit to kick‑start ‘small steps’ to rejoin
item.description: The UK has a shopping list of sectoral agreements it wants to come away with from next week's key and long-delayed EU-UK summit, part of the 'small steps' in a path that could eventually lead to membership.

item.title: [EU Observer] From pin-up calendars to the Istanbul Convention: Magyar’s U-turn, as Operation Purgatory reaches Orbán’s brother (Day 184 of the Tisza government)
item.description: Hungary’s political landscape is shifting dramatically as the new Tisza government challenges Viktor Orbán’s 16-year legacy. With Orbán’s brother facing detention, Fidesz support plunging to historic lows and corruption investigations gaining public backing, the country is entering a new political chapter. The government has also announced ambitious gender-equality measures, including stronger protections against domestic viol

item.title: [Euractiv] Let young Europeans shape policy, not just comment on it, says EESC youth chief [Partner Content]
item.description: Nicoletta Merlo, President of the EESC's Youth Group, wants youth participation to become a permanent feature of EU decision-making – from the first draft of a policy to the way Brussels spends its money

item.title: [DW] What have the talks with Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi achieved for Ukraine?
item.description: The first trilateral talks between Ukraine, the US and Russia in nine months have ended with an agreement on exchanging prisoners. Does this mark a genuine breakthrough and a step toward peace?

item.title: [Politico Europe] ‘Blind spot’ no longer: Austria targets Russian espionage with new law
item.description: “Austria’s lax approach to spies is now firmly a thing of the past," Foreign Minister Beate Meinl-Reisinger told POLITICO.

item.title: [DW] Hungary eases abortion restrictions in women's rights overhaul
item.description: The reforms mark a break the the conservative policies of former PM Viktor Orban. The controversial "heartbeat regulation" is to be scrapped and women are to be better protected against violence.

item.title: [Euractiv] EXCLUSIVE: Capitals consider sweeping review of migration pact in 2027
item.description: Next year will be dominated by elections in France, Greece, Italy and Poland

item.title: [Politico Europe] Trump’s snubbed COP — but he’s on everyone’s lips
item.description: Whether fretting about the Iran war — or picturing life without him — the U.S. president is looming large in the minds of politicians and campaigners at the global climate summit.

item.title: [EU Observer] Fastest EU citizens’ initiative ever pushes Brussels to end EU‑Israel trade agreement
item.description: Over one million Europeans back the ending of the EU-Israel trade agreement, in the latest citizen effort to hold European governments to account for their human rights commitments. Now the EU Commission has up to six months to respond.

item.title: [Financial Times] Jensen jeopardy will disrupt the AI industry
item.description: The Nvidia boss’s departure could deepen the technological rift between Washington and Beijing

item.title: [Euractiv] France to open international defence AI centre in 2027
item.description: Paris plans to seek NATO accreditation for the centre once revised rules allow it

item.title: [EU Observer] EU commissioner vows to use ‘all relevant tools’ to protect media freedom as Babiš public broadcasting bill alarms MEPs
item.description: MEPs spoke out against the Czech government's controversial broadcasting overhaul, while commissioner Michael McGrath said he would use “all relevant tools” to protect media freedom. Czechs in Brussels gathered outside parliament to protest.

item.title: [Euractiv] MEPs seek to hold EU firms liable over parts in Russian weapons
item.description: A draft letter pushes for mandatory cryptographic tagging of sensitive EU-made components

item.title: [Euractiv] IMF: Europe risks ‘spillover’ if bond turmoil persists
item.description: Fiscal consolidation must be coupled with productivity-boosting reforms, says Fund’s Europe director

item.title: [DW] UK court convicts 2 Iranian men of spying on journalists
item.description: A London court has found two Iranian citizens guilty of surveilling reporters for a Persian-language television station critical of Iran's government. One was also convicted of planning a violent attack against them.

item.title: [Euractiv] Putin suggests no Ukraine compromise in meeting with US envoys
item.description: The Russian president says he will not water down his demands to control parts of Ukraine

item.title: [Euractiv] The EU Data Act: Vehicle data access is changing, but is it working?
item.description: The EU Data Act and the revised Annex X to the Type-Approval Regulation are reshaping the rules governing access to vehicle data and functions. But how effectively are these rules working in practice? A new study prepared for FIA Region I by SBD Automotive examines how Europe’s leading carmakers are implementing these requirements, identifying persistent […]

item.title: [Politico Europe] Zelenskyy demands Europe become ‘regular part’ of Ukraine talks
item.description: EU still at odds over who should represent the bloc in any peace negotiations.

item.title: [Euractiv] Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns
item.description: Chief financial officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO

item.title: [EU Observer] Europe’s youth take to the streets as the post‑war promise of a better life breaks down
item.description: Europe's teenagers and students still believe in politics - but are turning away from parliaments and towards the streets. Hardly surprising, when the traditional milestones of adulthood – a degree, a stable job, a home and financial independence – are seem increasingly out of reach.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Ukraine meldet erneut Einschränkungen bei Starlink
item.description: Militäreinheiten hätten „erhebliche Beeinträchtigungen“ verzeichnet, ähnlich wie bei den im Oktober durchgesetzten Geschwindigkeitsbegrenzungen, sagte der ukrainische Präsident.

item.title: [Euractiv] MEPs push for national branding in EU food promotion campaigns
item.description: Parliament also called on the Commission not to discriminate against meat, dairy and wine in campaigns

item.title: [Financial Times] Ukraine says Starlink restrictions are back as US envoys land in Moscow
item.description: Army struggles to intercept Russian jet-powered drones, just as Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner meet Vladimir Putin

item.title: [Euractiv] MEPs target ‘sin industries’ in EU cancer plan vote
item.description: Right-wing attempts to water down the text were rejected

item.title: [Financial Times] Jensen Huang is gone. Will the AI industry pay the price?
item.description: Nvidia chief’s fall could unravel the web of financial dependencies that helped fuel the AI boom

item.title: [Euractiv] MEPs demand bigger EU budget to tackle emergencies
item.description: MEPs ask for €1.74 billion more than the Commission’s proposal

item.title: [Politico Europe] Feijóo wants to run Spain like a CEO. Not easy with far-right Vox on the board.
item.description: The center-right People's Party is casting itself as a business-like national manager, but a partnership with Vox threatens to push the PP in a more radical direction.

item.title: [Euractiv] E-who? Dublin summit grapples with who should talk to Putin
item.description: António Costa calls for a 'team effort' by Europe, the EU and NATO

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU will examine Israel association agreement after massive public petition
item.description: Organizers say the EU should suspend its trade and political dialogue with Israel.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU goes to Syria to talk business amid wider worries over lingering Russian influence and Jordanian attack
item.description: The EU is spearheading efforts next week to get Syria back on its feet, followed by an investment conference in Jordan. But Russian influence and recent lethal Jordanian fighter-jet attacks in southern Syria point to lingering issues.

item.title: [Financial Times] Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia chief executive
item.description: Shares in chipmaker slide after group says chief financial officer Colette Kress to take over as interim head

item.title: [Politico Europe] Ukraine Starlink speed restrictions in effect again, Zelenskyy says
item.description: Military units have recorded "significant disruptions" similar to the speed limits enforced in October, Ukraine's president said.

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘God, honour, fatherland’: Independence Day march shows Poland’s polarisation
item.description: Poland's 108th independence day commemorated the end of partition among foreign powers, but a far-right march joined by Polish president Karol Nawrocki reveals Poland may be threatened more by internal divisions than external threats.

item.title: [Financial Times] Maga architects blame Big Tech and AI data centres for midterms rout
item.description: Head of Heritage Foundation admits Republicans’ embrace of Silicon Valley and the effect of Donald Trump’s Iran war cost them votes

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Why can’t Europe offer Ukraine an alternative to Starlink?
item.description: Ukraine’s war effort depends heavily on two American tools: Starlink and Starshield. Both belong to Elon Musk’s SpaceX, and both can be switched off. Europe says it wants to reduce that dependence.

item.title: [Financial Times] Nvidia shares tumble on Huang exit
[DW] New trilateral talks on Ukraine war in Abu Dhabi: What to expect?
item.description: Ukrainian and Russian representatives last met in February for talks on ending the war, but the same sticking points remain. Ukraine continues to demand security guarantees, which is a non-starter for Russia.

item.title: [DW] Russia: Independent Novaya Gazeta shuts its Moscow newsroom
item.description: The investigative newspaper is closing its doors after Russian authorities labeled it a "foreign agent" and ordered it vacate its Moscow premises.
